Infra Pager: PagerDuty: P2 — GPU ECC corrected errors spike on gpu-node-3c (pool=gpu-prod-3), incident INC-20283 auto-created by Pager. Lots of repeats within last 6m.
Redwood Incident Bot: INC-20283 assigned to Maria Chen (primary on-call). Priority P2. Notifying eng-oncall.
Maria Chen: I'm looking — quick snapshot: ECC corrected count went from ~2/m to ~95/5m on node 3c, VRAM usage steady, temp up ~6C. No immediate OOMs.
Kevin Patel: I see related events: kubectl drain started on node gpu-node-3c ~10m ago? @Maria can you confirm whether this was manual drain or autoscaler?
Maria Chen: Negative, I don't see a manual drain request. K8s shows pod eviction started 12m ago for routine drain window. Might be overlap between eviction and long-running shader workloads causing ECC surfacing.
Samir Rao: Can you paste the PromQL you used?
Maria Chen: Sure: ```sum by(node) (increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[5m]))```
Samir Rao: Thx. For context our current alert is: ```expr: sum by(node) (increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[5m])) > 30 for: 5m``` which triggers often during drains.
Kevin Patel: That's the noise we've seen. Important: if alerts fire during intended drain, they flood oncall and mask real regressions. We should suppress using node labels or a drain metric.
Maria Chen: Agreed. For immediate mitigation I'm going to mute the alert rule for pool=gpu-prod-3 for 20m and escalate the manual investigation. Anyone object? :thumbsup:
Samir Rao: +1 mute. Also add temporary route to suppressed-channel so we still record counts.
Redwood Incident Bot: Alert rule muted by Maria Chen for 20m.
Maria Chen: Investigating whether kernel driver logs show ECC hardware churn. Pulling dmesg and nvlink logs now.
Infra Pager: Customer impact: 0.8% of inference requests in us-west saw transient latency spikes or 504s in last 15m. No broad outage.
Kevin Patel: Prioritization: P2 (customer-visible but limited). Main action items: 1) stop noisy alerts during planned drains, 2) adjust safe threshold or add suppression, 3) create dashboard showing drain + ecc + vram headroom.
Samir Rao: For suppression: we have a low-cardinality label k8s_node_state or node_annotation.draining=true set during drains. Could change alert to exclude nodes where node_annotation.draining=="true". Example: ```sum by(node) (increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[5m])) unless on(node) node_annotation_draining{draining="true"} > 30``` but PromQL doesn't support unless like that — better: use vector matching with absent/absent_over_time. Simpler approach: add `and on(node) (node_annotation_draining == "false")`
Maria Chen: Concrete rule change proposal (will prep PR after we stabilize): ```- alert: GPUHighECCCorrected
  expr: sum by(node) (increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[5m])) > 50
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "High corrected ECC errors on {{ $labels.node }}"
  # ignore nodes with draining annotation
  expr_notes: "Only fire if node_annotation_draining != \"true\""```
Kevin Patel: Two notable changes: raise threshold to 50 and increase for: from 5m->10m to reduce spike noise. Both will lower false positives during short drains. Fine by me.
Samir Rao: Also create a companion recording rule to surface ECC per-minute trends and include 95th percentile of memory headroom. Example record rules: ```- record: job:gpu:ecc_rate:5m
  expr: sum by(node) (increase(gpu_ecc_corrected_total[5m]))
- record: job:gpu:mem_headroom_pct:5m
  expr: avg by(node) (100 * (gpu_memory_total_bytes - gpu_memory_used_bytes) / gpu_memory_total_bytes)```
Maria Chen: I'm going to open a quick issue/PR with the proposed alert change, link dashboards, and request review from @Kevin and @Samir. I'll also add runbook steps (suppress during drain, check dmesg/nvlink, escalate to hardware if persistent).
Infra Pager: Note: node gpu-node-3c shows thermal excursion 78C -> 84C in 20m, fans auto-raised but still trending up. Keep monitoring.
Redwood Incident Bot: INC-20283 updated: investigation notes added.
Samir Rao: For dashboards: recommend a small panel set — ECC corrected rate (bars), VRAM headroom (line), node temperature (line), drain_annotation (state). Use template variables for pool and node. I'll draft a Grafana JSON snippet and attach to PR.
Kevin Patel: Also recommend an alert suppression policy: if node has active drain label OR kube_node_drain_state==1 then escalate to 'noise' route for 30m; else page primary. That reduces noisy pages during planned evictions.
Maria Chen: Updating incident notes: customer-impact small, mitigation: alert muted and thresholds increased, action: PR with alert + dashboard + recording rules, follow-up: add automation to set node_annotation.draining when we programmatically evict for autoscaler or rollout.
Oncall-bot: Handoff reminder — Maria (primary) will hand off to Kevin for the 20:00-04:00 window. Last check in 20m.
Kevin Patel: Taking Handoff at 20:12 UTC. Please paste PR link when ready. I'll watch the muted channel and ensure we don't regress.
Maria Chen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/monitoring/pull/612 — includes alert delta, recording rules, and a Grafana dashboard draft. Please review.
Samir Rao: Reviewing now. Also adding a quick playbook step: if ECC keeps spiking after drain completes, cordon node and run vendor diagnostics, collect nvlogs + nvml sample.
Maria Chen: Closing note: post-incident action items (PIA) — 1) implement drain-aware suppression (auto-set during safe drains), 2) re-evaluate ECC threshold across hardware families, 3) add VRAM headroom dashboard to A-Team runbook, 4) automation to tag drains from autoscaler.
Infra Pager: Incident INC-20283 resolved (no further spikes for 30m). All alerts un-muted.
Redwood Incident Bot: INC-20283 status changed to RESOLVED.
Kevin Patel: Thanks team. I'll merge quick fixes after Samir's review and schedule a longer audit for ECC thresholds next week. :slightly_smiling_face:
